utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Martinovic and Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Before we have the next witness, I would like to remind both parties that we will start this afternoon at 2.00, until 3.30, because at 4.00, there will be an initial appearance using this courtroom. Yes, Mr. Prosecutor. Are you ready for your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. I am ready. The next witness requested the following protective measures: Facial distortion and pseudonym. The motivation is that he, himself, and most of his next of kin are living in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: None, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And Your Honour, I must advise you that my questions, and I suggest that my witness's responses, will be relevant to Background, paragraph 7 to 10; Superior Authority, paragraph 14; General Allegations, paragraphs from 18 to 21; count 1, paragraphs 26, 27, 31, 34(a), (b); counts 2, 5, paragraph 34; counts from 9 to 12, paragraph 45.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Would the usher bring in the witness, please. While we are waiting for the witness, Mr. Prosecutor, would you please sent us that piece of paper so that we know who the witness is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: The registrar has it already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Would you please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may sit down, please. Examined by Mr. Poriouvaev:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, good morning. Your request for protective measures has been granted, and now you testify here protected by facial distortion and pseudonym. Your pseudonym will be Witness DD. Now you will be given a sheet of paper. You should read it, but not aloud, just to yourself, and if your name, date of birth are correct, you may say yes, and we'll proceed.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Witness DD, I will direct you to the events that happened in Mostar on the 9th of May, 1993, in the premises called Vranica building and in the surrounding area. What happened on the 9th of May in Mostar and what did you observe and get to know?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: On the 9th of May, I was in my apartment in the building called Vranica. Around 5.00 in the morning, I was awakened by strong shooting and explosions. I thought it was an attack by Serbian forces which were located on the eastern side of the town, that is on the surrounding hills, but when I got up, I realised the attack was coming from the western side. The civilians inside the building were panic-stricken. General commotion and chaos ensued. We didn't know what was going on. We headed for the basement. Certain parts of the building were hit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there many people in the basement by the moment you arrived there?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes, there were. People were gathering, afraid for their safety, because the upper parts of the building were under attack with infantry weapons and mines. So we sought shelter in the basement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were the people who gathered in the basement? Were there any military people among them?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: There were civilians of all ethnic groups; Muslims, men, women and children. In the basement were the quarters of the command of the BH army, as they called themselves. At the time, I didn't know how many soldiers there were because I had no access to those premises.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they firing back?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Later on, when the attack was well underway, they did fire, but with what, I don't know. That is, I saw them around the building. Those were soldiers armed with light infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just told that you saw them. As far as I understand, you saw the soldiers of the enemy formation. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Could you define that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I would like to understand your response: "That is, I saw them around the building. There were soldiers armed with light infantry weapons." Do you mean ABiH soldiers or some other soldiers?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: I meant inside the building, in entrances to the building. Those were not HVO soldiers. I couldn't really see. I didn't dare come to the window because there was shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD, some minutes ago, you explained to the Trial Chamber that your first impression was that the building had been attacked by the Serbs. When did you come to know that it was a different military force that attacked the building, and how did you learn it?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Well, that was obvious. Stories circulated immediately, because it was obvious the attack was coming from the western side. There were tensions in the town even before, and there were smaller skirmishes. During that day, one could hear demands made through a megaphone for soldiers to come out and surrender.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the people who were speaking through the megaphone identify themselves as belonging to some military unit?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes, they did. They said that the attack was being carried out by the Croatian Defence Council and they were demanding that the army surrender, that civilians come out. However, we, the civilians, didn't want to come out. Shooting hadn't stopped yet and we didn't know what was going to happen to us. We heard that certain civilians had already been taken to Heliodrom, to the stadium.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay within the basement?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: We stayed there until the 10th of May, until about noon, when the basement was attacked. Soldiers of the Croatian Defence Council advanced, started shooting, and they were already under our windows. They were shooting inside the basement, and a child was wounded. Water supply pipes had cracked and water was already flowing towards us. So we fled to the third, fourth floor, and we were waiting to see what would happen to us next.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why did you leave the building in the long run?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: We left the building -- the soldiers were shooting, throwing down their weapons. One of the civilians, one of the Croatian civilians inside the building had communication with the Croatian Defence Councils. And he made a sort of agreement and found out the details, so we came out, outside the school building, which was near the western wing of that building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the ABiH soldiers that were inside the basement? Did they also surrender?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes, one group did. I personally saw a group of soldiers who didn't want to surrender who remained behind after we left. One group of the soldiers was searching flats for civilian clothes, and they changed and followed us. They lined up in the courtyard of the School of Economics.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any people who were familiar to you among those ABiH soldiers?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: You mean among the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: No, I didn't know anyone from before. I wasn't in the army. I hadn't been in the army and I hadn't seen any of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what did you observe outside of the building?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Outside the building, we were met by the soldiers of the Croatian Defence Council. Jusuf, Juka Prazina, introduced himself. He said that we were prisoners now. And he also said that he wanted to lead the army. Why, I don't know, but he was then leading the Croatian Defence Council instead. On the spot, Juka Prazina separated Croatian civilians and told them they could -- they were free to go. As for Bosnian civilians, women, and children, they were separated into another group. And Muslim able-bodied men were put into another group yet and kept. In a file, two by two, he led us to the building across the old Velez stadium. I don't know what the name of the building is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did Juka's soldiers treat you, from the moment of your arrest until the moment, then, when you were taken to some building?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: As soon as we came out, mistreatment started. Juka Prazina himself was hitting one of the young men among us. He was pretending that he was not a member of the BH army. However, in his opinion, we were all being mistreated. There were many soldiers. Everyone was hitting people as they pleased.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were Juka Prazina's soldiers the only ones you saw in the area?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was only his unit. There were many, many soldiers all around the building. I saw them. I saw them holding positions in various sheltered spots. To what units they belonged, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any commanders apart from Juka Prazina in the area?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Outside the School of Economics, I didn't. At least, nobody said they were a commander. And I don't know -- wouldn't know to recognise ranks. It was just that Juka Prazina said that we were prisoners now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean not only in the place in the area of Vranica building. I mean the whole day of the 9th or the 10th of May, while you were in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes. Juka Prazina took us to the courtyard of that building whose name I don't know. There we were met by a larger group of soldiers, and among them was Tuta. There was also Misic. There were many commanders, many soldiers. Juka brought us there, and he reported to Tuta, and he said, "General, here they are. I've brought them," something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear this name "Tuta" before?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: I did hear that name personally, but I didn't know who or what he was, but I had Croatian friends who said things. I personally had not seen him before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what happened after Juka Prazina reported to a person called Tuta that the prisoners had been brought there?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Lots of things happened there in a very short interval. There were many soldiers, and mistreatment started. Juka - or, rather, excuse me, it's not Juka, it's Tuta. He was standing in front of us and saying that we would be executed right there on the spot. However, one of the soldiers intervened. I don't know whether he held a rank or not. He said, literally, that it was not the proper place to kill us. There was then an argument between them and some other soldiers got involved in it. Then Tuta said we would go to Siroki Brijeg and that we would all be executed, that we would all hang. He told the soldiers to drive us away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD, were there any concrete -- sorry, prisoners selected for being executed?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: We were counted. We were counted and ten of us were designated to be executed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was counting you?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: We were counted personally by Tuta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe the man that at least was introduced to you as Tuta?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes, I can. He was an older man, thin, long-haired, greying hair, wearing spectacles, in a uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Go on with the description of events that happened, as you just told us, in a short period of time while you were at that building.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: There I saw that Tuta recognised a person who was in that line, and I saw him hitting him with a Motorola, and the Motorola cracked, and then Juka stepped forward and said, "General, this is my soldier." I don't know what later happened to that man. We boarded a bus which was waiting for us at the building. We were being hit as we went through the gauntlet of soldiers. They kept hitting us until we boarded the bus. From there, we were taken to Siroki Brijeg, escorted by soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, I would like just to go into private session for some minutes, because we need some names here. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD, you just told the Chamber that on the way that you were taken from the building to the bus, you were beaten by soldiers. Whose soldiers were beating you?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: These were the soldiers of the Croatian Defence Council, but I wouldn't be able to tell you to which units they belonged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you beaten personally?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: I received a few blows.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were the soldiers that were escorting you to Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: These were the soldiers who had been in front of the building, that is, the Vranica building. I think that they were members of Juka's unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they mistreating you on your way to Siroki Brijeg? I mean --

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Not physically. However, they did threaten us. So psychologically, we were mistreated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you ever been in Siroki Brijeg before you were taken there on the 10th of May?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: No, I had never been there before, in Siroki Brijeg, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your impression of the first minutes there, of your arrival there?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you received, to make it more complete?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: We were brought in front of the civilian police building, and we were lined up there. We each had to identify ourselves, and the commander of that station also identified himself to us. Now I cannot recall his name. Our personal belongings were taken away from us there. We were taken to the basement. There were two cells there, measuring 3 by perhaps 1.5 metres, without windows. There was a kind of a block that was used as a window. In these first several days that we were there, soldiers would come in during daytime and nighttime, they mistreated us, they beat us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry. Do you remember any particular soldiers that were beating and mistreating you?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: I personally had known one of those soldiers from before. That was Romeo Blazevic. When he entered, he also recognised me. And he immediately started beating me right away. He had some kind of a stick with a -- coated with leather. It looked like a whip of some kind. I was sitting, crouching. And so he beat me. He beat my brother, and then he cursed us. And the other soldiers, I did not know. I saw them there for the first time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But were those other soldiers who were along with Blazevic also beating other prisoners?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: The soldiers who were coming would come either alone or in groups. Blazevic on that occasion had come alone. Later on, a man named Ivan and nicknamed Cikota, he beat prisoners, and it's terrible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What conditions of detention were there in the MUP station?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: The conditions? The cell itself where we spent three days was small and 20 men were put in there. There was no air. It was very difficult. We were let out to go to the toilet in the morning and in the evening, and we received food also twice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who was in charge of the MUP station? Who was commander of the MUP station? Who were the persons who were guarding you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. President, I object to that question and the form of the question. It's a compound question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. I will split this question into two questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please answer my first question. Who was in charge?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: At the MUP, I think that his nickname was Cane. I don't know his full name. I'm not sure. I think it was Cane. He did identify himself to us, but I did not remember the name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who was his commander?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who were the persons who were guarding you?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Those were members of the civilian police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they take prisoners outside of the cells for some purposes?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes. We went to work. We also swept the hallways of the police station building. And then, after we had been there for two days, 20 of us were taken to perform labour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of labour and where?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: There was a swimming pool in the centre of Siroki Brijeg, and it had been -- it had fallen into disuse, and we were cleaning it out to make it operable again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many days did you work on the swimming pool?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: We worked perhaps two, three days, two days. Then we were moved to the prison at Ljubuski.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: About three days. That was a military prison, and we were guarded by the military police. We were about 40, and we were all placed in a single cell and kept under lock. We stayed there for three days. On the third day, a soldier came and asked that the men who had worked at the swimming pool go back there, to Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that person who took "us" from Ljubuski back to Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: No. I cannot recall who that was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you -- sorry, where were you kept in Siroki Brijeg after Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: We were again taken back to the police station, and we stayed there for another ten days. We went on with work. And then we were transferred to the Tobacco Institute, that was part of the military barracks, and we were put up there. The headquarters of the Convicts Battalion was there, and there were some other units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was in command of the Convicts Battalion, do you know?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: According to the stories, it was Tuta. He was the commander of this unit or brigade or whatever it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see Tuta in Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes. I saw him. He once came to the swimming pool where we worked. I also saw him later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Several times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the situation -- situations in which you saw a person called Tuta?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Well, I saw him once at that Tobacco Institute. He came there. And once I saw him when we were taken to work, to dig a canal. He talked to the guards who were guarding us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did they treat you in the Tobacco Institute?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: At the Tobacco Institute, the conditions were better than at the station. We were not physically mistreated. Psychologically, we were. Soldiers would say all kinds of things in passing to us. On one occasion, soldiers came and took out three from among us. They were mistreated. They were beaten and questioned. Then this man, Ivan Cikota, came. He also mistreated the prisoners who had arrived there after us. They were brought from the Heliodrom, 10 to 15 men who had been brought there to help us with our job, which was digging.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just let's return a little bit. You were talking about three prisoners who were mistreated on some occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: If we go now into private session, Your Honour, could I ask the witness to give the names of those people, if he remembers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just informed the Trial Chamber that you were performing some digging jobs and some Heliodrom workers were taken to the tobacco station just to render you some assistance. What kind of digging works were you performing?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: This canal extended the length of a hill. In other words, we started at the top, and we were supposed to dig all the way down to the foot. It was an arduous job because it was very hot. We worked from morning until dusk. We only dug manually, of course. At first, we were assisted by civilian prisoners who were held at the Dobrkovici school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where that canal was located in Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: We went by bus there. We passed through the Dobrkovici village. And from there, we went on foot, and that's where Tuta's house was. I saw him there on one occasion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that that house belonged to Tuta?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Guards always said so. That house, the house was fenced off. We did not have access to it. We could only see the top part of it, the roof. And none of us ever approached that house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which was the occasion when you saw Tuta there?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Once when we were coming back from work, Tuta was probably waiting, and he was talking to the guards. This was -- this may have been August or July. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the canal digging finished?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: We worked on the canal for two to three months, and then the work stopped and we were reassigned to other jobs. Occasionally, we would come back and dig some portions of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What other jobs did you perform?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: We did various jobs; cleaning, sweeping around town. In the barracks, we did repairs. We did repairs in one house. We cleaned the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. drill grounds. We did loading and unloading in various storage houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever work for some certain persons?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes. We also worked in private houses, private homes such as Ivan Cikota's, for instance. We dug some sort of well. I also cleaned a stable of his. We dug some other wells, although I don't remember for whom. I only know that soldiers came to take us there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if other prisoners were involved in some jobs for -- in private estates?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes. Individual groups of about three to five men were taken away to perform various jobs. I know of a group which also worked on Zeljko's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what do you know about Cikota's family and Cikota, Cikota family?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: About his family, I know that one of their sons was killed. We arrived a little while after his death. He lived with his father and mother, with his entire family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD, did they ever pay you for the job on the swimming pool, on the canal, and for your job in private estates?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was your last place of detention?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: My last place of detention was Heliodrom. We were transferred there in December, and we were told then that we were being taken to be exchanged. We remained at Heliodrom until we were exchanged in March 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And my next question: You spent some time in different detention facilities; did you ever see the representatives of the Red Cross there?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: We saw them only at Heliodrom in December when we were registered. We didn't see them before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever registered before as a prisoner?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean by some humanitarian organisation, Red Cross or some other.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: No, no, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see ever military units deployed in Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: I did. I saw those Tigers. In addition to the local battalions, or what shall I call them, there were the Tigers, then the Gromovi, meaning Thunders. All of them were members of the HV, the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have different uniform from HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Basically, those were not different uniforms, but they had distinct arm patches depicting tigers as a sign of their brigade. Then also in passing, I saw certain soldiers carrying weapons. They had their airplanes in which they were sitting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness DD.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have completed my examination-in-chief in my allotted time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any cross-examination? Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: It may be trucks, not airplanes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, I did not have my headphone on. Did the witness mean trucks instead of airplanes? Did I catch that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's a correction from the interpreters. But you could clear it up if you still have doubts on this point. Cross-examined by Mr. Meek:

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Could I ask the assistance of the usher, please. For the record, I am handing the usher what has previously been marked and admitted as P11.18. It's a map of Mostar. Please hand it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Meek, you said it is previously marked, which might give some hint to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, I will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I mean, this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, the map is a map of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Have you got a clean map?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: This is a clean map, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Could you show the witness the map, please, on the ELMO. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD, good morning.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My name is Mr. Christopher Meek, and I am one of the attorneys for Mr. Mladen Naletilic, and I would like to ask you a few questions. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you do not understand one of my questions, will you please tell me so that I can rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD, is it true that you grew up in Mostar your entire life?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in front of you on the screen is a map of Mostar. Do you recognise that?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: The image is too dark, but I can see that it's Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If it would help you, Witness DD, you can take the map in front of you for the moment and take a look at it.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you take a pencil, please, or a pen, and please mark where the building is located where you were living on the 9th of May, 1993, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Meek, you understand that this witness is under protective measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: May we go into closed session. I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will go to the closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This exhibit is D1/29.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It should be under seal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD, after you arrived at the location of the house across from the Velez stadium, you've indicated that you saw Juka along with an individual by the name of Tuta; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: May the ELMO be lowered, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before that day, you had never seen this individual, correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: I never saw him before, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you have, since your release from the Heliodrom in 1994, given two statements to the Office of the Prosecutor for this Tribunal; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD, the first statement you gave was approximately the 28th of April, 1997. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Witness DD, would you agree with me that, back in April of 1997, the events which had occurred during the war were fresher on your memory then than they were three years later, in the year 2000?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: I wouldn't quite agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived at the location by the house at Velez stadium, you indicated that Juka -- excuse me, that the individual who you say is Tuta had taken a Motorola and struck one of the other prisoners; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you -- how far away was this other prisoner when that occurred?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: A couple metres to my right side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you tell in your statement that the Motorola broke or shattered?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: It fell out of his hand, and whether it cracked from the blow or from hitting the ground, I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. But in any event, the Motorola actually fell to the ground and, in the process, it broke at some point, correct? I think, for the record, the witness answered, "Yes," but it's not on the screen. Did you answer, "Yes"?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: I said I don't know whether it cracked from the blow or from hitting the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it at this point or immediately thereafter that Juka approached this individual Tuta and talked with him?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in your first statement that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor, you indicated that Juka approached this man and called him Tuta, correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Well, he said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Poriouvaev.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: The name is protected. It should be redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we should have this name redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay, I'm sorry. I apologise. I didn't realise that individual.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, Juka told Tuta to stop the beating. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: In my second statement, I said that the gentleman, Mr. Naletilic, said -- that is, Juka told Tuta, General Tuta, he said it was his soldier. What arrangements they had between the two of them, Juka and Tuta, I don't know. I don't know why all this. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And you just now mentioned that in your first statement, Juka addressed this gentleman as "Tuta"; but in your second statement, three years later, Juka addressed this gentleman as "General Tuta." Can you please explain what the difference -- why the difference from your first statement to your second statement, if you can.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Well, look. At the time when I was giving my first statement, I was trying hard to forget certain things. I don't know if you can understand this. But the more you delve into this, the more the memories come back. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's fine. That's fine, Witness DD. Would it also be true that in that period of time between 1997 and 2000, that you spoke with other people from Mostar or the area of Bosnia-Herzegovina about the events which occurred in '93 and early '94?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: It could have happened, but I did not talk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, it would be a fair statement, would it not, Witness DD, that in that period of time after the war, you saw TV clippings about this gentleman, Mr. Naletilic, and you also read newspaper articles and saw his picture in the newspaper? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Excuse me, could you repeat that. I didn't hear very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. During the time after you were released from the Heliodrom, you saw Mr. Naletilic in the newspaper, and also on TV.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is also one of the ways that you discovered what his real name was, besides the guards telling you. Correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Well, not quite correct. Once you got to know him makes no difference whether you see pictures or not. As I said, I saw the gentleman a couple of times during the period of my detention.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to talk to you a moment about that. Didn't you only see him three times total?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: A couple of times, I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To make sure I'm not confused, the first time you saw him was on May the 10th. Correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then can you tell me when the second time that you saw him? When was that?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: That was at the swimming pool. Also in May. Which date it could have been, I can't recall. While I was working at the pool, he visited once to inspect how the work's coming along.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he in civilian clothes at the swimming pool that day in May, Witness DD?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: No, he was wearing a military uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then the last time that you saw Mr. Naletilic would have been the day that you were coming back from digging a canal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on that day, you were in the bus with the other prisoners; correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: We hadn't boarded the bus just yet. We were lined up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that occasion, I believe in your statement you indicated that this gentleman had on casual, civilian clothes, correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that. I remember saying that. But I remembered later that he wasn't wearing civilian clothes, if that is so important to you. He could have just as well worn civilian clothes, but when I came here, I gave a solemn oath to tell the truth, and I think that a statement may be changed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD, both the statements you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor, you read and signed those statements, did you not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Meek, if you are going to use this statement so extensively, why not furnish this statement to the witness? You have to be fair to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will always be fair to the witness. The witness understands exactly -- I don't need to show the witness the statement to refresh his recollection at this moment. He remembers the statement, and so therefore I do not believe I need to show it to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the question is not whether you believe it or not. The question is that this Chamber has made a ruling on this point, that if you want to use the previous statement, you have to show it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honour. I see it's the 11.00 break. Would this be the appropriate time to take the 11.00 break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we will resume at 11.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD, I'd like to take you back a moment and ask you to describe, please, the house that you mentioned earlier that was the old house across from the Velez stadium where you were taken.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Well, this was a house with a big yard, with hedges around, and I think that all the paths were covered with pebble. I do know they were gravelled and -- I cannot recall the house very much because I did not take a good look at it, but I remember the hedges, and the -- they were lining up the paths.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Witness DD, can you tell me, to the best of your recollection today, how many minutes it took you to walk from the building to this location?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: I believe about ten minutes; perhaps a bit more, a bit less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Another quick question is once you arrived at that yard that you've described, how much time elapsed between your arriving and the incident where you say Mr. Naletilic hit [redacted]-- or hit another person with the Motorola?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Can you perhaps clarify this for me? What do you mean "how much time"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once you arrived at the location of the house, then how much time went by before you observed the incident with the Motorola?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Not much, but time was the least consideration at that time. I did not follow the time, but it wasn't -- it wasn't very much time. It happened really quick.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Real quickly too: You mentioned that you were in the building and you heard a voice on a megaphone asking you to come out; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Now, what building are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The building that you were located in on the 9th of May and the 10th of May.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise the voice through that -- that was speaking through that megaphone that day?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I would ask the usher to hand the witness what has been previously marked as Exhibit D1/22. Thank you. First I would just ask the witness to look at the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, have you looked at that photograph?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise that? Do you recognise that location?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but it seems to be a very private conversation between the counsel and the witness. We don't see the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Please put it on the ELMO. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The first thing is that you have to inform us what is this document about. The second thing, I don't know yet, but I suspect that it will identify the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: No, it will not. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: It will not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the ELMO, for the record, is a photograph which has been previously marked as D1/22. And I would ask the witness, do you recognise that photograph?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: No. To me, this building has no significance whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That's all I want to ask the question about that exhibit. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Could you lower the ELMO, please. Somebody please lower the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD, you have already testified about the incident with Juka Prazina stopping the beating of one of the prisoners. You remember that?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, you testified that Mr. Naletilic had picked out ten people, and you were one of those ten. Correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then there was an intervention by another HVO officer who was present, was there not?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was this HVO person, he was an officer, correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: In my opinion, yes, I believe that he was an officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And part of your opinion, is it correct, is based on the fact that this man had bodyguards with him?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after Mr. Naletilic had picked the ten people, you being one of those ten, this officer also intervened, did he not?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this officer not only intervened, but actually shoved Tuta. There was some shoving and quarrelling. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes, they developed a quarrel, and then other soldiers stepped in. I believe that they were bodyguards. I think that they were the bodyguards of both men, and they kind of lowered the tensions. I could not see it very clearly because we had to keep our heads down, lowered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So besides these two different people who intervened to help stop the beating and save your lives, did anybody else intervene in that moment?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD, you have described a person by the name of Romeo in Siroki Brijeg. Correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe this person for the Trial Chamber, please, physically his description.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: The main feature, to my mind, was his shaven head. He was about my height, perhaps a little bit shorter. 35 to 40 years of age.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know this individual before you arrived at Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did know him. He was the owner of a coffee bar which I patronised. He also knew me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how long had you known this individual, Romeo?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: A fairly long time. We used to live on the same street. That was a long time ago. So we were neighbours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you described the incident where Mr. Romeo, this individual Romeo, would come to the cell, is that correct, and take people away?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: No, no, no. He was not taking people away. I don't believe that I said that Romeo was taking people away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I stand corrected. You described an incident where this Romeo came into the cell; correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: He was in a military uniform, camouflage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which unit he was from or with?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he come alone that night?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: He entered our cell by himself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Witness DD, what time was that, approximately, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: I believe it was night-time. I did not have a watch, and the concept of time is vague at that time, at least, to me it was. But it was during the evening hours, but perhaps night-time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And were the civilian guards that you've talked about, were they present then?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Not in the cell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was this Romeo -- was he drunk that night?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: I had no way of telling. I don't know whether he was drunk or on Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. drugs. I wouldn't be able to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he appear to be out of control, to you, that night?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: He was angry. He was enraged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he looking for any specific person, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: He entered through the door, and he first turned to me, because he knew me, and he started hitting me with this leather whip. We were sitting down, and he was standing, and that's how he hit me with this rod or --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the leather whip, about how long was this leather whip, the length?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Not very long, 30 to 40 centimetres, perhaps. It was like weaved leather, and I think that it had some kind of a metal ball at the top.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where this individual by the name of Cikota was when this occurred?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Romeo ever say that somebody had sent him to do this, that he had been ordered to do this by anybody?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: He made no confessions to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you make a complaint to the civilian police that were guarding you about this incident?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if anybody in your group did?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: I don't believe so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've testified, Witness DD, about your digging of a canal. Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe the guards who took you in the mornings and stayed with you while this canal was being dug.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to describe it because the people who were guarding us changed during that labour, because we went on working there for a long time, several months. These were soldiers in uniform, armed with automatic rifles, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Maybe I'll be a little more specific. Were they older, older soldiers, or were they younger soldiers?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Well, there were some older soldiers, and then there were some who were younger, in their 30s. Those who were guarding us at the swimming pool were all older ones. They called themselves home guards. They were kind of a reserve.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did sometimes the home guards go with you to the work on this digging of the canal? Or did they just stay at the swimming pool area?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: These were two separate jobs. In other words, we were not in a position to do both jobs at once. We first finished the swimming pool. Then we went on -- proceeded with the digging of canals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I understand. But when you went to the digging of the canals at a later time, did some of the older home guard go with you from time to time?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to gain knowledge of any of the names of these home guards?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Perhaps some did introduce themselves to us, and we could overhear what they called each other. But I did not remember any of that. It didn't seem important to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at the swimming pool, when the home guards were guarding you, were they armed?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes, they were, with automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've indicated that during your entire stay at the various facilities, you were first in Siroki Brijeg. Correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You went to Ljubuski for several days?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you returned to Siroki Brijeg to the MUP station again?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just for several days.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: About ten days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you went to the Tobacco Institute in Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes, we were transferred to the Tobacco Institute.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, you were transferred to the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've indicated, I believe, both in your statements and in your testimony, that you were not physically mistreated, only psychologically mistreated. Is that a fair statement? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: In the beginning, there was some physical mistreatment. But later on, it stopped.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just several more questions, and I'll be finished, Witness DD. I appreciate your testifying today. I want to go back to the incident with the individual that got hit with the Motorola. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right before that happened, didn't you observe this individual step towards Mr. Naletilic?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Mr. Naletilic called him -- he probably had known him from before. I overheard a part of the conversation that took place between them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the part of the conversation which you heard led you to believe that they knew each other from the past. Correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you don't know in what relationship they may have had in the past. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm almost finished, Witness DD. Since you said you heard some conversation between Mr. Naletilic and this individual, can you tell us, to the best of your recollection today, what was said?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: I remember that Tuta said, "Where have you been, blood brother?" That I remember quite well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's the extent of what you remember of the conversation between this man and Mr. Naletilic?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I don't think I have any further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. And I guess there's no cross-examination from Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence of Mr. Martinovic has no questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, only one question. Re-examined by Mr. Poriouvaev:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD, in your testimony today - this is page 14, line 9 - you stated that on one occasion, you saw Tuta in tobacco station. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Just I wanted to clarify the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Judge Diarra has two questions. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. Witness DD, before you arrived at the tobacco station, whilst you were at the police station, you said that Tuta himself picked out ten people and threatened to execute them. Was this threat carried out, if only on a few of these people, or was it just a mere threat that was not carried out?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: As I said during my evidence, they were not executed. What happened was a quarrel ensued between Tuta and another, I believe he was an officer, and he pointed out that this was not a place where we should be executed. So I don't know whether Tuta would have gone on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Now, about Tuta's house, you said that you never actually entered the house, that you only saw it from afar, from a certain distance. Looking from that distance, were you able to see prisoners working inside the house from where you were standing?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: No. We were not able to see that. This was a hilly area, and the house was surrounded by a fence. We had no access there. We had no idea what was going on inside the house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. These were my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Diarra. Any questions out of Judge Diarra's questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, just one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You'll be have to be very quick.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Further cross-examination by Mr. Meek:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DD, Judge Diarra has made me think of something. That is, can you tell the Trial Chamber the name of the village that you were digging the canal towards?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: I know the name of the village through which we passed by bus in order to get to that area. That's the village of Dobrkovici. And then the road that we were taking went down the hill to the town of Listica, which means that the village was not down at the bottom of the hill, it was up at the top.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's the village name you just mentioned. Was there another village that you had forgotten the name of?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD
utterances.text: I'm not aware of there being one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, witness. Thank you for giving your testimony. When the usher pulls down the blinds, you may leave. At this stage, are there any documents to tender from both sides?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. I have no exhibits to tender today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I would ask that the map, marked now D1/29, which Witness DD made two marks on and a line on, that be admitted. And the previous -- the picture that I showed Witness DD had been previously marked and admitted as D1/22 so I'm not sure whether I need to give that a new number or not. I don't believe I should. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections to the document D1/29?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I don't have any objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. It is admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Bos, are you handling the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Yes, I'll be handing the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could you give me some notice who will be the next witness? I mean give me some indication? What is the number on that list you provided us on the 16th of October?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I think he will be the next witness on the list. I won't reveal his name at this stage because we are in public session and he has requested some protective measures, this witness. He would like to have facial distortion and a pseudonym. Well, I'm not sure which list you are referring to, so that's why I'm not -- I don't have the witness list in front of me. I can give you the sheet with the name. Maybe that's easier to clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Bos, does the testimony of this witness have any difference with the previous one?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, this witness will testify on a lot of events which are repetitive. We've heard testimony on most of the events he will testify about, so I intend to go through this testimony very swiftly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We understand that in certain jurisdictions, that one witness is no witness, but we have heard the same incidents for many times.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of this, Your Honour, and this is going to be the last witness in the row in this respect, but, yes, again, I can go as swiftly as possible. But we would like to call this witness, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: While we're waiting for a moment, perhaps I can assist. It may assist the Chamber. I advised Defence counsel several Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. days ago that if we conclude these witnesses this week, as you may recall, another Prosecution witness by the name of Prelec, Marko Prelec, has been kind of floating around. We skipped him because of scheduling issues a couple of times. I had advised counsel that, if we have time, we will try to get to him then tomorrow. It seems to me, on the pace that we're on, we very well will get to him tomorrow, and might even start him this afternoon, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. After consultations among the Judges, we have decided that we are going to hear this witness on the condition that you have to go through with him as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That was my intention. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Yes. As I said, the witness has requested facial distortion and a pseudonym.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: None, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. While the witness is being led in, let me just refer to the relevant paragraphs in the indictment. The Background, paragraphs 7 and 10; Superior Authority, paragraph 14; General Allegations, paragraphs 18 through 21; count 1, paragraphs 26, 27, 31, 34(a), 34(b); counts 2 to 8, paragraph 44; counts 9 to 12, paragraph 45.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness nodded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: May I proceed? Examined by Mr. Bos:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you're going to be shown a sheet of paper which shows your name and the name of your pseudonym. Could you look at this sheet of paper and confirm that this is your name and the date of your birth.

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as you can see, you have been referred to as Witness EE. So in your testimony, I will refer to you as Witness EE. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: I can understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honours, for the first part, I would like to go into private session for a few questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I have been referring to the 9th of May. Can you briefly tell us what happened on the 9th of May.

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: On the 9th of May, around half past 3.00 in the morning, fierce shelling began on our building. We woke up. We didn't know what was going on until we went out into the hallway. We found there tearful women and children who started screaming, "We're being attacked. We have been attacked by the Croatian Defence Council."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long did the attack last?

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: The attack continued the whole day of the 9th of May, and on the 10th of May, we surrendered, around 2.30 or 3.00. I couldn't say precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us more about the surrender? What happened when you surrendered?

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: When we surrendered, we were ordered to leave the building and stand in front of the School of Economics. We came out, with our arms raised, to the yard outside the School of Economics. Men were separated from women, Muslims were separated to one side, and the Croats had been separated already. There were soldiers there, including Juka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were these soldiers, were these all HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: They were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned a man by the name of Juka. Did you know this man before?

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: Not personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you did know him, though, although not personally?

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: I knew him from the newspapers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what his full name is?

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: I know; Jusuf, Juka, Prazina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall from which unit this Juka was?

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: Juka?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: Juka was on the HVO side. I don't know which unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the members of Juka's unit, did they have any distinctive -- first of all, let me ask how did they look like and did they have anything distinctive on them, on their clothes?

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: They were wearing yellow strips or ribbons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you testified that the men and women were separated. And what happened next? Where were you -- were you taken somewhere?

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: Once separated, we were lined in two rows and taken to the area outside the ministry. Up there at the ministry, we were met. Up there, I saw Mr. Tuta. We were lined up in two rows, and we stood there for a while.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that you saw a man by the name of Tuta. Could you describe this man, please.

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: I could. Grey, grey-haired with a beard, and it's the man sitting here in the courtroom right now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any other people while you -- when you arrived there at the Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: No, just him. I recognised only him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you recognised him. Had you met the man named Tuta before?

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: No, I hadn't. That was the first time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But how were you then so certain that it was Tuta?

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: Tuta? How was I sure? Well, I saw him in the newspapers. He was -- how shall I tell you? I didn't know him personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just said that you saw the same man here in the courtroom. Could you describe the man in the courtroom you've been referring to?

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I can. Can I point him out?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please do, and just give a description on how he looks like and where he sits.

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: This gentleman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please describe him here in the courtroom, for the record.

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: He has grey hair and beard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could the witness please sit down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have to sit down, I'm sorry. All right. Grey hair and a beard.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: May the record reflect that the witness has identified the accused Mladen Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that you saw Mr. Tuta when you arrived at the Ministry of Defence. Please tell me what happened.

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: Down there we were also standing, lined in two rows. Mr. Tuta beckoned to one. [redacted]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, please don't refer to names unless I ask you but -- please continue but don't refer to names any more. So he was -- yeah, please continue where you were. So he was --

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: I saw him starting to hit this gentleman. He hit him with a Motorola and said, "Where have you been, blood brother?" That's all I heard and saw. As for the rest, I couldn't see well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see where this person was hit with the Motorola?

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: Yes, this person was struck in the face.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anything happen with the Motorola when this person was hit?

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: The Motorola, it remained in his hand. I didn't see whether it was damaged or not. I know that the man was bleeding, though.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened after this?

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: After that, an argument -- dispute occurred between Tuta and another man. And at that moment, the bus arrived. And then Mr. Tuta said, "Take those shits up there. They will hang at Siroki Brijeg." And when we were boarding the bus, a group of soldiers started to hit us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, did this man, Tuta, also speak with a man named Juka?

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: Tuta, when he hit that gentleman, Juka came at that moment and said, "Don't touch him any more." And he sort of separated this gentleman from Tuta. He took him slightly to one side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did Tuta, after speaking to Juka, say anything else? Did he say anything else to the group?

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: I couldn't hear well. I don't remember him saying anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to observe everything what happened before the Ministry of Defence in a clear way?

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: I couldn't see everything clearly. All I could see clearly was that, because I was standing close by when he was hitting this gentleman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why couldn't you not observe everything else clearly? Was there any particular reason for that?

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: We had to keep our arms behind our back and our heads down. We had to look down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified at one moment you were taken to a bus and that you were assaulted when you were walking towards the bus. Who assaulted you?

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: We were assaulted by some members of the Croatian Defence Council. I don't know which unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you taken to?

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: We were taken to Siroki Brijeg, to the prison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened when you arrived at the prison? What was the name of the prison? Do you recall what building it was?

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: It was the MUP building, the MUP. We were lined up there. They confiscated our cigarettes, identity cards, lighters, shoelaces, trouser belts. And then we were taken down to the cells.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were people being beaten while you were lined up in front of the MUP station?

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: I only saw one man who was struck by a member of the MUP, because he recognised him. He asked, "Are you an operative worker?" He said, "No, I'm an intelligence man." Then this MUP member hit him several times after that. And after that, we were taken away, taken down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you were taken down. Where were you taken to?

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: We were taken to the basement, to cells in the basement of that building. There were two cells, and that's where they put us and locked Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. us up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, do you recall a man by the name of Kazim Mesic?

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is he?

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: He was already down there when we arrived. That's why I remember him. He had come before we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just looking at the transcript, could you please spell his last name, or spell his full name, please.

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: K-A-Z-I-M M-E-S-I-C.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When you were detained at the MUP station, were people ever mistreated?

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: Yes, they were. They were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us who mistreated you?

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: I can. It was Romeo Blazevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know this person?

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please explain to us what happened when Romeo Blazevic came into your cell.

utterances.speaker: Witness EE
